sentences.text: Wannchampsus is an extinct genus of neosuchian closely related to but distinct from true crocodilians.
The genus is based on the partial skull and lower jaw fossil SMU 76604, with associated remains including forelimbs and vertebrae.
The skulls are described as low, broad, and small, with the largest specimen estimated at 64 mm in length.
The genus Wannchampsus was described by Thomas Adams in 2014.
The type species W. kirpachi was named in honor of Wesley Kirpach for his role in discovering and excavating the type specimen.
Features of the skull and vertebrae suggest that the known individuals were subadults.
Wannchampsus is classified within the family Paralligatoridae.
Fossils of Wannchampsus have been found in Lower Cretaceous rocks in north-central Texas, United States, specifically in the Twin Mountains Formation near Stephenville.
Wannchampsus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, between 119.57 and 110.1 million years ago.
